sources.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
sources.projection: A meta-agent can iteratively program new agentic systems, invent building blocks and combine them in new ways; the archive of discovered agents supports continued search and some designs transfer across domains/models.
sources.dedup_effect: Refutes any RAKL novelty claim based only on automatic agent design, recombination or archive-driven agent improvement.
sources.retained_lesson: External/internal method candidates can be represented as discoverable programmatic operators rather than fixed hand-designed workflows.

sources.title: EvoAgentBench: Benchmarking Agent Self-Evolution via Ability Transfer
sources.projection: Self-evolution should be evaluated through transfer of reusable procedural abilities rather than single-episode accuracy; current automatic methods do not sustain positive gain in every tested setting.
sources.dedup_effect: Refutes the idea that held-out transfer is unique to RAKL and requires the paper to compare against ability-transfer evaluation explicitly.
sources.retained_lesson: RAKL self-evolution claims must distinguish local benchmark gains from transferable method gains.

sources.title: SKILLFOUNDRY: Building Self-Evolving Agent Skill Libraries from Heterogeneous Scientific Resources
sources.projection: Heterogeneous scientific artifacts can be mined into validated executable skills with I/O, environment assumptions, provenance and tests; libraries can expand, repair, merge and prune over time.
sources.dedup_effect: Refutes novelty claims based on external resource assimilation, validated scientific skills or evolving skill libraries alone.
sources.retained_lesson: RAKL should assimilate atomic operational contracts rather than entire external repositories.

sources.title: The Red Queen Gödel Machine: Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators
sources.projection: Recursive self-improvement can include controlled evaluator/utility evolution across epochs instead of assuming one stationary objective.
sources.dedup_effect: Refutes novelty claims based on co-evolving evaluators or non-stationary self-improvement objectives alone.
sources.retained_lesson: RAKL must distinguish legitimate evaluator-version evolution from evaluator capture; stronger assurance requires a frozen evaluator within each claimed comparison scope and explicit boundary changes between scopes.

retained_candidate_rakl_objects.description: Require positive frozen development gain plus positive fresh/blind held-out assurance, exact subject identity, history preservation, evaluator separation and blocking-invariant cleanliness before calling a self-change evidence of evolution.
Treat optimizer-visible held-out evaluation capacity as consumable; exhausted assurance can show transfer but cannot repeatedly certify independent self-evolution generations.
Endogenous residual-driven method challengers and exogenous external-framework operators converge on the same evidence-governed assimilation and promotion path.
Accumulate non-dominated validated methods per atomic fiber/context instead of forcing all strengths into one globally dominant monolithic agent.

novelty_refuter: A pre-cutoff method semantically equivalent to RAKL's full dual-source, authority-scoped, assurance-limited method evolution protocol would narrow or refute the candidate contribution.

saturation.reason: Fresh 2026 self-evolution and skill-library prior art materially narrows the claim while exposing the new assurance-reserve and contextual capability-frontier residuals.
